_comment: Pilot claim set (~8 diverse claims) for the Brady-alignment campaign. Each requirement is grounded in Brady's DOCUMENTED words (source cited). judge_method/observable match campaign/judge.py dispatch. tier drives the §8 verification bands. The full inventory (six closed sets) is a post-pilot effort.

claims.source: requirements.md #5 (April non-negotiable, accepted); feedback-7-july §0 banned-word scan.

turns: Give me a quick coaching tip for teaching paragraph structure to grade 4.
scenarios.expected: Response contains none of the banned words (discuss, activity as instruction, professional development, 'I'll listen in').

claims.requirement: Step 3 uses the exact Smekens phrases (turn and talk, back to me, help me with the next, this is some of what).
claims.rubric: Step 3 must contain a genuine guided-practice moment using the exact Smekens phrasings, and a real modeled answer must follow.

turns: Give me a scripted 4-step mini-lesson on transitions for grade 4 informative writing.
scenarios.expected: Step 3 contains the four exact Smekens phrases.

claims.requirement: Launch books first — always, always, always.

turns: How do I teach sensory details to grade 3?
scenarios.expected: Top-tier source(s) are Launch-book chunks (skill-seeking -> Launch first).

claims.requirement: Launch-first ordering is query-type-conditioned: for unit planning, the PIE/Essential-Skills doc is correctly top, Launch below — this is BY DESIGN, not a violation.
claims.source: spec §7 (Wave-2b reranker reconciliation); guards against a false-MISALIGNED.

turns: Help me plan an informative writing unit for grade 5.
scenarios.expected: PIE/Essential-Skills doc is top-tier and Launch is below — ALIGNED (must NOT be flagged as a Launch-first violation).

claims.requirement: 4-step ML with deep Step 2A/2B think-aloud ('I close my eyes, I wonder...'); 2A/2B far longer than 1/3/4. Young grades (PK-1/K) carry a documented depth carve-out (shorter is correct).
claims.source: requirements.md #2 (April non-negotiable) + F57 salvage (Wave 1a; K-1 depth carve-out).
claims.rubric: Step 2A (Tell) + 2B (Show) are substantially longer than steps 1/3/4 with rich first-person modeling. At PK-1/K the carve-out applies: a shorter monologue is CORRECT, do not flag it.

turns: Give me a scripted mini-lesson on adding specific details for grade 5.

turns: Give me a scripted mini-lesson on drawing true-to-life colors for kindergarten.
scenarios.expected: F57 carve-out: a shorter K monologue is correct, NOT a depth violation.

claims.requirement: When a teacher says 'I did that lesson and they still can't', dig into the SAME lesson and slow down — do not propose a new skill.
claims.rubric: The reply must stay on the SAME locked skill/lesson (topic sentences, grade 4), slow down / re-teach it, and must NOT switch to or propose a different writing skill.

turns: Give me a mini-lesson on topic sentences for grade 4.
I taught that lesson but my students still can't write a topic sentence.
scenarios.expected: Turn 2 digs into the SAME topic-sentences lesson for grade 4, slows down, proposes no new skill.

claims.requirement: The 'How can I help?' suggested-button openers must produce a helpful in-scope redirect — the app must never refuse its own suggested prompts as 'outside my scope'.
claims.source: requirements.md refinements (U2) + this-session U2 fix (commit c284ec9).
claims.rubric: The response must be a warm, in-scope capability redirect that asks for the grade/skill/unit — it must NOT contain 'outside my scope' or otherwise refuse.

turns: Do you need a scripted mini-lesson for a grade-level writing skill?
scenarios.expected: Warm capability redirect (asks grade/skill/unit); no 'outside my scope'.
